items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: We went down to Australia, and there was a nice tour with Coleman Hawkins, the Teddy Wilson Trio with the bassist Arvell Shaw

ctx.x: There was a lot of fun and everything that I had with Al -- a lot of things. But anyway, that began to sort of wane, his popularity... A lot of things that he began to do wasn't very good for his career. Finally, about 1960, we began to do spotted engagements, one here, one there, we'd do three weeks here, we'd do a month here.

One time we did a trip to Australia, which was a very nice thing. I think this was in the early 60's. We went down to Australia, and there was a nice tour with Coleman Hawkins, the Teddy Wilson Trio with the bassist Arvell Shaw -- I've forgotten who the drummer was with Teddy Wilson. It also included Sarah Vaughan and her trio. Also, Dakota Staton... It was just a mammoth show. We played about three or four cities in Australia. And we played in these big stadiums, I guess they were soccer stadiums or something --…
But as I said before, Al's thing began to wane. It got so whenever he had an engagement, he would call me, and I would go with him if I wasn't doing anything else.
